# Printer setup by chat: UX review and proposal

Reviewed on 2026-09-23 against branch `jusprin-newui` at commit 886098514b, by reading the code and the four screenshots Kenneth attached. Nothing was run live: the review is of what the code renders and when, not of a recorded session.

Summary for a cold reader: the printer setup chat was built as a three-phase state machine (identify a printer, then add it, then optionally connect it), and the chat is a helper bolted to the side of that machine. Each phase has its own screen chrome, its own copy, and its own single tool the model may call, and the transitions between phases happen outside the conversation with no message in the thread. That is why the screens feel like two products at once. The fix is not copy edits. It is to make the conversation the only surface, make the app's phase changes into tool calls the assistant makes with confirmation cards, and delete the chrome that grew up around the phases.

## 1. How it is built today

The panel is one React page (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx`, the `printerPanel` branch at lines 405-566) driven by one C++ class (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp`).

- **Three modes, one tool each.** `ConversationMode` is Add, Change, or Connect. `session_tools()` at PrinterConversation.cpp:161 gives Add exactly `printer_identify`, Change exactly `printer_change`, and Connect nothing. Once a printer is added, `profile()` at line 306 removes all tools for the rest of the session.
- **Adding is not a tool.** `printer_identify` only draws cards. The actual add is a page action ("Add this printer" chip, `PrinterChipRow` in `components/PrinterPanel.tsx:151`) that reaches `add_proposed_printer()` at PrinterConversation.cpp:787. On success it sets `m_added`, pushes state, and returns. It posts no note and starts no model turn, so the thread goes silent while the screen above it changes.
- **Connecting is a form.** `components/PrinterConnection.tsx` is a 100-line form with six connection states, each mapped to its own sentence. It renders in a region above the thread (App.tsx:486-492, capped at 60% height). The model gets the connection state as JSON pasted into its system prompt (`printerInstructions.ts:112-126`) and is told "use the form above this conversation. There are no tools in this phase."
- **The receipt is on Home.** When the panel closes after an add, `close_panel(&m_facts)` carries the added printer's facts to `ShellController::refresh_home` (ShellController.cpp:580), which sends a `printer_added` event, which the Home page draws as the strip in screenshot 1 (`HomeUI/src/App.tsx:122-146`).

## 2. Kenneth's five issues, traced

### #1 The duplicate "Creality K1 added" card on Home

- **What it is:** `HomeUI/src/App.tsx:11-24` builds the strip text from `FactProvenance`, an internal enum with values settled, assumed, changed. The word "assumed" on screen is that enum leaking. The strip has a "Change" link whose object is unclear and an "x" to dismiss it. Directly below it the real card for the same printer glows once (`printer-card-added` animation).
- **Why it exists:** commit a975c79be6 says the receipt was added so Home "names it plainly, and says what the card assumed". The panel had just lost its pinned summary card, and the receipt was moved to Home rather than into the thread.
- **Fix:** delete the strip and the `printer_added` event (`HomeHost.cpp:48-64`, `ShellController.cpp:169-183` and `580-590`, the `AddedPrinterInfo` protocol type). The receipt belongs to the assistant's own reply after the add tool succeeds: "Done. The Creality K1 is set up with the 0.4 mm nozzle it ships with." Keep the one-shot card glow on Home, which already exists and needs no strip.

### #2 "Choose your printer so JusPrin can prepare prints for it. You can connect it afterward."

- **What it is:** a hard-coded title and explanation in the chrome, `App.tsx:458-459`. The same prepare-versus-connect distinction is taught to the model at `printerInstructions.ts:26` and `49-51`, so the model also explains it unprompted ("Adding lets JusPrin prepare prints for that model; it does not connect to the machine").
- **Why it exists:** the developer needed the user to understand the phase machine, because the phases are visible.
- **Fix:** delete the title and explanation. The assistant's opening line already asks the only question that matters. Connecting is something the assistant offers at the moment it becomes possible, in its own words, with a chip to accept or decline. The user never has to hold the two concepts apart.

### #3 "Your printer has been added" panel above the thread

- **What it is:** `PrinterConnection.tsx:38-49`, rendered by App.tsx:486-492 above the message list. In screenshot 2 the thread's last message is still the assistant refusing a 0.7 mm nozzle, while the panel above says the printer is added. The add happened in `add_proposed_printer()` with no message, and the model's tools were silently removed.
- **Fix:** make add a mutation tool (`printer_add`) that requires approval. The existing approval-card path (`ToolActivityCard`, `renderActivity`, `PrinterChangeCard`) already draws a card in the thread with two buttons and returns the result to the model. The printer card with "Add this printer" and "Not this one" becomes that approval card. After approval the tool result reaches the model, and the model writes the receipt and offers the next step. Nothing renders above the thread.

### #4 "Go to Home" that looks like a title

- **What it is:** `PrinterConnection.tsx:99` is a bare `<button>` with no class, so it renders as plain text. The same line switches its label between "Go to Home", "Done", "Back to printers" and "Not now" depending on state. Five more bare buttons sit in the same file: "Refresh printers" (line 93), "Sign in to Bambu" (line 85), and "Printer settings" (lines 52 and 96). This breaks the design-system rule in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` that every control comes from a token recipe.
- **Fix:** delete the button. The panel already has a back control in the header. When the assistant says "You're all set", it offers a "Done" chip in the thread, the same chip component the add flow uses.

### #5 The connection form above the chat

- **What it is:** the form in `PrinterConnection.tsx:58-95`, opened by "Connect printer" from either the receipt or a Home card. In Connect mode the model has no tools (PrinterConversation.cpp:163-164) and cannot see the result of a connection attempt until the user types again, because `connection_start` (line 726) refreshes state but starts no turn.
- **Fix:** make connecting a tool with a confirmation card that carries the credential fields. The model calls `printer_connect` with the device or address it has worked out. The card in the thread shows what it is about to do and the one field it needs (LAN access code or API key). The credential goes from the card to C++ with the approval decision and never into the tool arguments, the result, or the thread. The result ("connected", "no response after 30 s", "wrong code") comes back to the model, which explains it and suggests the next thing to try. A read-only `printer_connection_status` tool lets the model see which matching printers are on the network and whether the person is signed in, so it can say "I can see a P1S on your network" instead of the user picking from a dropdown. The full form stays as a fallback behind an "Enter the details myself" chip.

## 3. The pattern behind all five: the app runs the flow, the chat narrates it

Kenneth asked for the places where the "app developer" mentality shows in the code. These are the concrete ones.

1. **Phases decide what the model may do.** `session_tools()` (PrinterConversation.cpp:161-168) and `profile()` (line 306): one tool per mode, zero after add. The model cannot take the user from "which printer" to "ready to print" on its own.
2. **Phase transitions bypass the model.** `add_proposed_printer()` (787-819), `connection_start` (726-739), and `manual_setup` (742-773) all change state and push it to the page, but none posts a note or starts a turn. Compare `reject_proposal()` (914) and `choose_candidate()` (877), which do both. Only the transitions the developer thought needed "guidance" got it.
3. **The tool refuses in the app's vocabulary.** PrinterConversation.cpp:525-528: `setup_finished: "The printer is saved. Connection is handled by the person's connection controls."`
4. **The prompt teaches the model the screen layout.** `printerInstructions.ts:40-41` ("point to Choose printer manually at the top of the panel"), `49-51` ("the success screen offers Connect printer and they can also connect later from Home"), `115` ("using the form above this conversation. There are no tools in this phase"). The model is being used as a help desk for the app's own chrome.
5. **The page is a view of the state machine.** `PrinterSessionPayload` (`bridge/protocol.ts:448-459`) carries `mode`, `canAdd`, `added`, `manualApplied`, `connection`, and `facts` with provenance. App.tsx reads these to decide which chrome to draw (`connectionPhase`, `offerManualPrinterSetup`, lines 408-411) and then draws different headers, titles, links and regions per combination (lines 447-461, 486-499).
6. **Status strings are written for someone who knows the architecture.** "File sending configured", "Status unknown" (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:220-226`); "Connection test succeeded. File sending is configured; live printer status is not shown here. Starting a print is a separate action." (PrinterConnection.tsx:54); "This credential is never sent to the AI assistant" (line 90); "Where supported, you can send files directly from JusPrin" (line 49); "· assumed" (HomeUI App.tsx:22).
7. **Manual escape hatches are top-level chrome.** "Choose printer manually" / "Set it up myself" in the header (App.tsx:452-456) and "Connection settings" (line 461) are always visible, so the fallback competes with the primary path.
8. **Layout differs per phase.** Add takes the whole workspace (`app--printer-setup`, App.tsx:407, ShellController.cpp:602), Change and Connect take the narrow rail. The back control has three labels: "‹ Back to Home", "‹", and "‹ Printers"/"‹ Your printer" (App.tsx:448-451).

The unifying principle for the fix: **the only things on the panel are the back control, the thread, and the composer.** Everything else is either a message from the assistant, a card the assistant's tool call produced, or a chip the assistant offered.

## 4. Other issues found

Ranked by how much they hurt.

1. **The assistant is deaf to outcomes.** After an add, a connection attempt, a wizard return, or an undo, the model learns nothing until the user types. The connection phase is worst: `connection_refresh` polls every second (PrinterConnection.tsx:30-34) and the page re-sends the whole system prompt each time the JSON changes (App.tsx:184-190), but no turn runs. A user who watches "Connecting…" turn into "The printer did not respond" gets a form message, not help.
2. **Focus ring around the heading.** Screenshot 5 shows a purple box around "Connect your printer". `PrinterConnection.tsx:26` calls `focus()` on the `h1` with `tabIndex={-1}`, and the global `:focus-visible` rule (`styles.css:53-55`) draws the ring. Goes away with the form.
3. **New content appears at the top.** In the connection phase the receipt and form sit above the thread and the thread's last message stays stale (screenshot 2). Chat readers expect the newest thing at the bottom.
4. **Thread lines are far too wide in Add mode.** Screenshot 2 shows assistant text running about 1,400 px. `--printer-setup-width` caps the column but not to a reading width.
5. **The leave confirmation is about the developer's state, not the user's.** "Leave this conversation? What you said here will be lost." (App.tsx:462-485) fires when a proposal card is showing. The words in a throwaway setup chat are worth nothing to the user. Either drop the dialog or keep the session alive so nothing is lost.
6. **Home nags every printer to connect.** `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:220-226` gives every named printer "Not connected" and a full-width "Connect printer" button (screenshot 1), including printers that have no network at all. A never-connected printer should be quiet; "Connect…" belongs in the card's menu, and status text belongs only on printers that have been connected before.
7. **The wizard fallback returns to a status sentence in the chrome.** "No new printers were added. Your existing printers are available from Home." (App.tsx:460) after cancelling OrcaSlicer's wizard. This should be the assistant saying "No problem. Tell me the brand and model and I'll find it."
8. **A nozzle mismatch sends the user to OrcaSlicer's settings dialog.** PrinterConnection.tsx:52. The panel already has a `printer_change` tool with a confirmation card. The assistant should say "Your printer reports a 0.6 mm nozzle but it is set up as 0.4. Update it?" and use that tool.
9. **The composer promises what the assistant cannot do.** Connect-mode placeholder is "Ask for help connecting your printer" (`printerWords.ts:58`), but the assistant cannot act on the answer.
10. **Two agent instances and two documents per panel** (`PrinterPanel.cpp:63-77`): defensible engineering, but it means the printer chat never remembers anything across openings. If the user comes back tomorrow to connect, the assistant starts from zero. Worth deciding whether a printer's conversation should persist per printer.

## 5. Proposed design

### 5.1 The flow as the user experiences it

One panel, one width, one back control. Everything below is in the thread.

```
Assistant  Which printer do you have? Tell me the brand and model, or share a
           photo of its label.
User       anycubic 3
Assistant  That's the Anycubic Kobra 3. I'll set it up with the 0.4 mm nozzle
           it ships with. If you've swapped it, tell me the size.
           [card: Anycubic Kobra 3 · 0.4 mm nozzle    (Add this printer) (Not this one)]
User       taps Add
Assistant  Done. The Kobra 3 is ready and you can slice for it now.
           If it's on your Wi-Fi I can also send files straight to it.
           Want to set that up?           [Yes, connect it] [Not now]
User       taps Yes
Assistant  The Kobra 3 is managed by its own software on the printer. What
           address do you use to open it in a browser? It's usually the
           printer's IP, like 192.168.1.20.
User       192.168.1.42
Assistant  [card: Connect to 192.168.1.42 · API key (if it asks for one) [____]   (Connect) (Cancel)]
User       taps Connect
Assistant  Connected. Files you slice for the Kobra 3 can go straight to it.
           You're all set.                 [Done]
```

For a Bambu printer the assistant calls a status tool first and says "I can see a P1S on your network named Workshop. To connect it I need the access code from the printer's screen: Settings, then Network, then LAN Mode." The card then has the one code field.

Escape hatches are chips the assistant offers when they help ("Browse the full printer list" when more than three models match; "Enter the connection details myself" when the assistant's guess fails twice), plus the same two entries in an overflow menu in the header for people who want them immediately.

### 5.2 What changes in the code

**Tools replace page actions and phases.** One printer session, no `ConversationMode` gating of tools. The tool set:

| Tool | Class | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `printer_identify` | read-only | as today: checks names against the list, returns facts |
| `printer_add` | mutation, approval card | the printer card with Add / Not this one; on approval saves the printer and returns the saved printer |
| `printer_connection_status` | read-only | matching printers on the network, sign-in state, saved address, current state |
| `printer_connect` | mutation, approval card | card states the target and holds the one credential field; on approval runs the existing `connect_printer` / `connect_host`; result is the outcome, never the credential |
| `printer_change` | mutation, approval card | as today |

Preconditions move into the tools as errors the model can read ("that printer is not saved yet"), which is what `preflight_tool` already does for `printer_change`. The `m_added` / `m_connection_name` phase flags, `session_tools()`, and the `setup_finished` refusal go.

**Credentials ride on the approval, not the arguments.** Extend `tool_decision` with an optional field carried host-side only: the page sends the access code with the approve decision, `PrinterConversation::execute_tool` reads it from the activity's decision, and it is never written into `arguments_json`, `result_json`, the note stream, or persistence. This keeps the guarantee the current footnote promises without the user having to read a footnote.

**Outcomes reach the model as notes plus a turn.** Every backend outcome that today only calls `session_changed()` posts a fact note and starts a turn, the way `reject_proposal()` already does: add succeeded, connection verified or failed (the 30 s timer in `OrcaPrinterBackend::connection` fires this), wizard returned with or without printers, undo done. The `connection_refresh` polling loop in the page goes; the backend already knows when the attempt resolves.

**The page loses its chrome.** In `App.tsx` the printer branch keeps: the header with one back control and an overflow menu, the message list, the composer. Delete: the title and explanation (458-459), the manual-setup header links (452-456, 461), the `manualApplied` status line (460), the connection region (486-492), the "Need help" line (493-496), the `PrinterChipRow` outside the thread (533-542), the leave dialog (462-485). Delete `components/PrinterConnection.tsx`; the credential card is a new small component rendered through `renderActivity` beside `PrinterChangeCard`. Delete the Home strip and the `printer_added` event.

**The prompt describes a goal, not a screen.** Rewrite `printerInstructions.ts` as one prompt: the person wants their printer set up so they can print; identify it, add it with their confirmation, then offer to connect it if that can help them, and stop when they say they are done. Remove every sentence that names a button, a screen, a form, or a phase. Keep the rules that encode real constraints (one question at a time, never guess a model from shape, never substitute a nozzle size, never ask for a credential in chat).

**One layout.** Pick one width for Add, Change and Connect. The wide workspace with the thread capped at a reading width (about 720 px) is the better choice, because photos and printer cards need room. One back label.

### 5.3 Copy that has to change regardless

| Today | Proposed |
|---|---|
| Creality K1 added · 0.4 mm · assumed, Textured PEI Plate · assumed, … | (assistant) Done. The Creality K1 is set up with the 0.4 mm nozzle it ships with. |
| Choose your printer so JusPrin can prepare prints for it. You can connect it afterward. | (deleted) |
| Your printer has been added. You can now prepare prints for X. Connecting is optional. Where supported, you can send files directly from JusPrin. You can set this up later from your printer's card. | (assistant) The X is ready. If it's on your Wi-Fi I can also send files straight to it. Want to set that up? |
| Connection test succeeded. File sending is configured; live printer status is not shown here. Starting a print is a separate action. | (assistant) Connected. Files you slice for the X can go straight to it. |
| Not connected / Status unknown / File sending configured (Home card) | nothing for a never-connected printer; "Connected" or "Can't reach it" for one that was |
| This credential is never sent to the AI assistant. | (card caption) Stays on this computer. |
| Leave this conversation? What you said here will be lost. | (deleted) |
| Choose printer manually / Set it up myself (header) | overflow menu: Browse the full printer list; and a chip when the assistant needs it |

### 5.4 Tests that carry the current design

These tests in `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` assert the phase machine and will need to be rewritten rather than kept green: "each mode offers exactly its own tool", "Add saves once and shows a receipt before returning Home" (744), "an old Add message cannot submit connection credentials" (777), "connect later opens without agent tools" (1067), "connection assistance receives instructions without printer mutation tools" (1714). The shell harness checks at `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:534-561` and the Home receipt checks in `tests/jusprin/test_home_host.cpp` assert the strip and the phase transitions. The Agent UI tests `PrinterPanelApp.test.tsx` and `PrinterConnection.test.tsx` cover the chrome that goes.

## 6. Suggested order of work

1. `printer_add` as an approval tool, add outcome posted as a note plus turn, chip row and Home strip deleted. This alone fixes #1 and #3.
2. Chrome removal and one layout. Fixes #2 and #4 and the focus ring.
3. `printer_connection_status` and `printer_connect` with the credential card, outcomes posted, `PrinterConnection.tsx` deleted. Fixes #5.
4. Prompt rewrite and copy table. Home card quieting.
5. Decide on per-printer conversation persistence.

## 7. Questions for Kenneth

- Should the printer conversation persist per printer, so "connect it later" resumes rather than restarts?
- Is the full-width workspace the layout for all three entry points, or should Change stay in the rail?
- OrcaSlicer's wizard as the "browse the full list" fallback: keep, or build an in-thread list picker later?

# Handoff: make the printer setup chat the only surface

Written 2026-09-23 against branch `jusprin-newui` at commit 886098514b. This file is a working document. Do not commit it, do not add it to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Kenneth tracks unfinished work through untracked files in `git status`.

Companion: `printer-setup-ux-review.md` in the same directory holds the UX review that led here, with screenshots described and every finding traced to a file and line. Read it first if anything below feels unmotivated.

## 1. What this is about

JusPrin (this fork of OrcaSlicer) lets a person add, change, and connect a 3D printer by talking to an AI assistant in a panel on the Home screen. The panel was built as a three-phase state machine (identify, add, connect) with a different screen, different hard-coded buttons and copy, and a different single tool for the assistant in each phase. The assistant is not told when phases change. The result is a confusing mix of chat and forms.

The job: rebuild the panel so the conversation is the only thing on it. Every button the user taps is a reply the assistant suggested. The assistant performs adding, changing, and connecting itself through tools. The one exception is a password-like credential, which is typed into a small card so it never passes through the assistant.

## 2. Decisions Kenneth has already made

Do not reopen these.

1. The assistant decides which reply buttons to show. Tapping a button sends its text as the user's message. Nothing else is wired to a button.
2. "Add this printer", "This one", "Use this", "Keep / Set" and "Undo" all become reply buttons the assistant offers, not hard-coded controls.
3. No memory across openings. Each time the panel opens, the conversation starts fresh, as today.
4. Full-window layout for all three entry points (Add, Printer settings, Connect). No narrow side-column mode.
5. OrcaSlicer's own printer wizard stays as the "browse the full list" fallback. Do not build an in-chat list picker.

## 4. Target behaviour

### 4.1 What is on the panel

Top: one back arrow, and a small overflow menu with two entries, "Browse the full printer list" (opens OrcaSlicer's wizard, today's `manual_setup` action) and "Open printer settings" (OrcaSlicer's printer settings window, today's `open_printer_settings`). Middle: the chat thread, capped at a reading width. Bottom: the composer with its Photo button.

Nothing else. No title, no explanation paragraph, no region above the thread, no button row between thread and composer, no "Go to Home", no "Leave this conversation?" dialog.

### 4.2 Reply buttons

The assistant ends a message with suggested replies. The page draws them as a row of pill-shaped chips directly under that message, in the same column as the assistant's text, left-aligned, wrapping to more lines as needed. Only the newest message in the thread shows chips. Tapping a chip sends its text as the user's message through the existing `user_message` path, so the chip text appears as the user's bubble on the right and the chips disappear because a newer message now exists. Typing is always allowed; chips are a convenience, never the only way to answer. Chips are keyboard-reachable (Tab, Enter).

User       anycubic 3
Assistant  [printer_identify runs; the printer card with its picture appears]

User       Yes, add it

User       Connect it

User       192.168.1.42
Assistant  [printer_connect runs; the credential card appears]

Bambu: after "Connect it", the assistant calls `printer_connection_status`, sees the candidates on the network, and says "I can see a P1S named Workshop on your network. I need the access code from the printer's screen: Settings, then Network, then LAN Mode." with a chip per candidate if there is more than one, then calls `printer_connect` with the chosen device; the card has the access-code field. Only LAN-mode printers are offered (see section 11). If no LAN printer matches, the assistant explains how to turn on LAN mode on the printer and check it is on the same network, and offers ( Enter the connection details myself ).

Change (opened from a card's "Printer settings…"):

```
Assistant  This is the Creality K1. Tell me what changed on it, or ask
           anything about it.
User       I put a 0.6 nozzle on it
Assistant  Set the K1 to a 0.6 mm nozzle? Every project that uses it will
           slice for 0.6 from now on.
           ( Yes, set 0.6 mm )  ( Keep 0.4 mm )
User       Yes, set 0.6 mm
Assistant  [printer_change runs] Done, the K1 is set to 0.6 mm.
```

There is no undo row. "Put it back to 0.4" is a sentence the assistant handles with the same tool.

Connect (opened from a card): the same as the Add conversation from "Connect it" onward, opening with "Let's connect the Kobra 3. What address do you use to open it in a browser?" or, for Bambu, with the status check.

Fallbacks the assistant offers as chips: ( Browse the full list ) when more than three models match or nothing matches, ( Enter the connection details myself ) when a connection has failed twice. Both are also in the overflow menu. The reply text for these is handled by the assistant calling `printer_manual_setup` or `printer_manual_connection`, which open OrcaSlicer's wizard and printer settings window respectively, then post a note with what came back.

## 5. Design details

### 5.1 How the assistant sends reply buttons

Recommended: a fixed last line in the message text.

The instructions tell the assistant: "When you want to offer the person answers to tap, end your message with one line of the form `Choices: first | second | third`, two to four short choices, each under 30 characters. Offer choices whenever the answer is a yes or no, a pick from a few options, or a confirmation. Do not offer choices when you need free text such as an address."

The page (`MessageList.tsx`) strips a trailing `Choices:` line from an assistant message when rendering and draws the chips instead. While a message is still streaming, hide any trailing partial line that starts with `Choices:` so it never flashes. No C++ change, about 30 lines of TypeScript plus CSS. If the assistant omits the line, the person types; nothing breaks.

Why not a tool: `AgentHost::handle_agent_tool_call()` completes the current assistant message on every tool call and `continue_after_tool()` always starts a follow-up assistant message after the result. An `offer_choices` tool would therefore end the message and provoke an empty or repetitive follow-up unless `AgentHost` learns a new "this tool ends the turn" concept. `OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp` line 309 also answers unanswered function calls with a refusal on the next request, so a dropped call is not free either. Only go the tool route if the eval in section 7.4 shows the line format is unreliable, and then teach `AgentHost` the concept explicitly rather than special-casing a tool name.

Preconditions are tool errors the assistant can read, following the pattern in `preflight_tool()` today.

### 5.3 The credential card

`printer_connect` is the only tool that shows an approval card, and it reuses the existing approval path unchanged except for one addition.

- The registry marks it as requiring approval, exactly as `printer_change` is today. `handle_agent_tool_call()` proposes it, the coordinator holds it Pending, the page draws it.
- The page renders it through `renderActivity` in `MessageList.tsx` (the seam `PrinterChangeCard` uses today) as a new small component: a line stating the target ("Connect to Workshop (P1S)" or "Connect to 192.168.1.42"), one password-type field labelled "Access code" for Bambu LAN or "API key (if the printer asks for one)" for hosts, a caption "Stays on this computer.", a primary Connect button and a plain Cancel button. Only LAN printers reach this card (section 11), so it always has a field.
- Connect sends the existing `tool_decision` with `decision: "approve"` and one new optional field, `input: { "credential": "..." }`. Cancel sends `reject`.
- In `AgentHost::handle_tool_decision()`, if `input` is present, store it in a new `std::map<std::string, json> m_decision_inputs` keyed by `actionId` before calling `m_tools.approve()`. Expose `std::optional<json> take_decision_input(const std::string& action_id)` that removes and returns it. The session executor in `PrinterConversation` calls it while executing `printer_connect`. That is the entire host change: about 15 lines.
- The credential never enters `ToolActivity::arguments_json`, `result_json`, any note, any envelope from host to page, or persistence. Write a test that asserts exactly that (section 7.2).

### 5.4 Connection outcomes reach the assistant

`connect_host()` is synchronous: its result is known when `printer_connect` executes, so the tool result carries it ("verified" or the failure message from `HostAttempt`).

`connect_printer()` (Bambu) is not: `OrcaPrinterBackend::connection()` resolves the attempt later, when push data arrives or the 30-second timer in `connection()` expires. Handle it like this:

- `printer_connect` returns `{"state": "connecting"}` immediately. The assistant is instructed that "connecting" means say one short line and wait; the app will report (section 11).
- `PrinterPanel::on_pump()` (the existing 33 ms timer) calls a new `PrinterConversation::tick()`. While a Bambu attempt is in flight (`m_backend.connection(name).state == "connecting"`), `tick()` polls at most once per second. When the state leaves "connecting", `tick()` posts a note with the outcome in words, for example "Connection to Workshop verified." or "Connection to Workshop failed: the printer did not respond.", calls `m_host.printers_changed()`, and calls `m_host.start_turn()` so the assistant replies at once.
- This replaces the page's one-second `connection_refresh` polling loop and the instruction-resend loop in `App.tsx` lines 184-190.

The same note-plus-turn pattern applies to the two OrcaSlicer windows: after `printer_manual_setup` and `printer_manual_connection` return, the tool result says what happened, so no extra note is needed there.

### 5.6 The prompt

Rewrite `printerInstructions.ts` as one prompt with three parts: a fixed core, a mode-specific opening context, and the facts.

Core, in substance: You are JusPrin's printer assistant, talking to someone who may never have used a slicer. The goal is that their printer is set up so they can print, and connected over the network if that helps them and they want it. Plain language, one to three short sentences, one question at a time, say where to find any answer you ask for. Ask before adding, changing, or connecting; the person's yes is the confirmation, then call the tool. After a tool result, say what happened in the person's terms. Never say something is done before the tool says so. Then the `Choices:` line rule from 5.1 with two examples.

Keep from today's rules, because they encode real constraints: start with the model only, do not ask for plate or filament; one fits means identify it, two or three means ask which with a chip each, more than three means one narrowing question or offer the full list; a name that is the start of several models is not one model; a photo names a model only from a readable label; never substitute a nozzle size; `alreadyYours` means the model was saved before, not this machine; a credential is never asked for in chat; "connecting" means wait for the app's report; a timeout means no response, not a wrong code; a nozzle mismatch reported by the printer is something to offer to fix with `printer_change`.

Delete every sentence that names a button, screen, form, or phase.

Mode context: Add adds "The person is adding a printer. Printer list: …, on the network now: …". Change and Connect add "The printer this is about: name, model, nozzle, nozzles it ships, spools, connected". The opening lines in `printerWords.ts` `opening()` stay, with the Connect opening changed to ask the first question rather than advertise the form.

metadata:

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 08293464-543a-44de-9266-25cac34b4e36

---

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
  clicks. Escape does not close them.
- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.

**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.
Consequence: fixed-width popups ellipsize *more* on Windows. Do not assume the 4/5
factor makes Windows text smaller. Mono text goes the other way (Courier New is
narrower than Menlo), so the chip itself comes out 346 px on Windows vs 353 on Mac.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]],
[[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

Exit code 1
# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. Set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object if another JusPrin
is already running. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` and
`colour` are optional and cosmetic for that same read.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.

## Unit tests

`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (Catch2, GUI build). They cover announce JSON,
control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.

## Agent id

Registered as `jusprin-fake-bambu`. `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` uses that
id in place of `bbl` when fake mode is on. No other upstream file is involved.

## 12. Implementation notes (2026-09-23, uncommitted on jusprin-newui)

Steps 7.1, 7.2, 7.3 and 7.5 are implemented, plus the card wording of 5.7. What differs from sections 5 and 11, and what the live runs showed:

- **Routing.** The coordinator hands every tool with `ToolExposure::Printer` to the session executor, instead of a list of handlers. Each new tool still needs a `ToolHandler` value, a registry definition, and an argument checker in `valid_arguments()` (`ToolRegistry.cpp`), which rejects any tool it does not know. Section 11.5 missed that last one.
- **Credential hand-off.** The input is kept until the approved action runs on a later tick, and dropped in `continue_after_tool()` whether or not it was taken.
- **No thread-width token.** The panel's column is already capped by `printerSetup.contentWidth`, so `threadWidth` was not added.
- **Choices parsing** also accepts "Choices:" at the end of the last sentence. The model often leaves out the line break.
- **Discovery starts once per session.** `printer_connection_status` calls `prepare_connection()` only the first time. Starting it again restarts discovery, and the model then never found the printer.
- **`printer_connect` accepts the printer's name as `deviceId`.** The model passes the name the person used. The error lists the valid ids.
- **Backend fix, `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer`.** Connecting a LAN printer that is already selected used to fail with "The selected printer changed". Re-selecting it disconnects and reconnects, and GUI_App's local-connect handler clears the selection one event turn later, after the reconnect. The printer is now deselected and selected again on the next turn. The backend's own harness test interrupts one turn later to match.
- **When the assistant asks first (Kenneth, 2026-09-23).** A change the person states plainly is made at once. The assistant asks first only when it is guessing: the model from a photo or a vague description, a nozzle size nobody said, or which printer on the network. After this change, three live runs got every Change case right. Two of three still added a printer without checking the assumed nozzle.
- **A second add of the same model in one conversation is refused** (`already_added`). The model had added a duplicate printer on a second "yes".
- **Model reliability under the old ask-first rule, gpt-5.4-mini, 10 live runs.** The model saved without waiting for yes in 6 Change flows and 2 Add flows, even with "ask, then stop" in the prompt. It sometimes passes the network printer's name as `printerName`. It twice ended a reply with no words, which the panel hides.
- **Not yet verified.** The modal wizard opened from `printer_manual_setup` (11.6), the Moonraker/OctoPrint path live, and the page's look in the real app.

## 4. Target behaviour

### 4.1 What is on the panel

Top: one back arrow, and a small overflow menu with two entries, "Browse the full printer list" (opens OrcaSlicer's wizard, today's `manual_setup` action) and "Open printer settings" (OrcaSlicer's printer settings window, today's `open_printer_settings`). Middle: the chat thread, capped at a reading width. Bottom: the composer with its Photo button.

Nothing else. No title, no explanation paragraph, no region above the thread, no button row between thread and composer, no "Go to Home", no "Leave this conversation?" dialog.

### 4.2 Reply buttons

The assistant ends a message with suggested replies. The page draws them as a row of pill-shaped chips directly under that message, in the same column as the assistant's text, left-aligned, wrapping to more lines as needed. Only the newest message in the thread shows chips. Tapping a chip sends its text as the user's message through the existing `user_message` path, so the chip text appears as the user's bubble on the right and the chips disappear because a newer message now exists. Typing is always allowed; chips are a convenience, never the only way to answer. Chips are keyboard-reachable (Tab, Enter).

### 4.3 The conversations

Add:

```
Assistant  Which printer do you have? Tell me the brand and model, or share a
           photo of its label.
User       anycubic 3
Assistant  [printer_identify runs; the printer card with its picture appears]
           That's the Anycubic Kobra 3. I'll set it up with the 0.4 mm nozzle
           it ships with. Is that right?
           ( Yes, add it )  ( I changed the nozzle )  ( Different printer )
User       Yes, add it
Assistant  [printer_add runs]
           Done. The Kobra 3 is ready and you can slice for it now. It runs
           its own software on the printer, so I can also send files to it
           over Wi-Fi if you like.
           ( Connect it )  ( Not now )
User       Connect it
Assistant  What address do you use to open the printer in a browser? It's
           usually its IP address, like 192.168.1.20.
User       192.168.1.42
Assistant  [printer_connect runs; the credential card appears]
           If the printer asks for an API key, enter it here. Otherwise just
           tap Connect.
           [card: Connect to 192.168.1.42   API key [________]   (Connect) (Cancel)]
User       taps Connect
Assistant  [the outcome comes back; the assistant replies]
           Connected. Files you slice for the Kobra 3 can go straight to it.
           ( Done )
User       Done
Assistant  [printer_setup_finish runs; the panel closes]
```

Bambu: after "Connect it", the assistant calls `printer_connection_status`, sees the candidates on the network, and says "I can see a P1S named Workshop on your network. I need the access code from the printer's screen: Settings, then Network, then LAN Mode." with a chip per candidate if there is more than one, then calls `printer_connect` with the chosen device; the card has the access-code field. Only LAN-mode printers are offered (see section 11). If no LAN printer matches, the assistant explains how to turn on LAN mode on the printer and check it is on the same network, and offers ( Enter the connection details myself ).

Change (opened from a card's "Printer settings…"):

```
Assistant  This is the Creality K1. Tell me what changed on it, or ask
           anything about it.
User       I put a 0.6 nozzle on it
Assistant  Set the K1 to a 0.6 mm nozzle? Every project that uses it will
           slice for 0.6 from now on.
           ( Yes, set 0.6 mm )  ( Keep 0.4 mm )
User       Yes, set 0.6 mm
Assistant  [printer_change runs] Done, the K1 is set to 0.6 mm.
```

There is no undo row. "Put it back to 0.4" is a sentence the assistant handles with the same tool.

Connect (opened from a card): the same as the Add conversation from "Connect it" onward, opening with "Let's connect the Kobra 3. What address do you use to open it in a browser?" or, for Bambu, with the status check.

Fallbacks the assistant offers as chips: ( Browse the full list ) when more than three models match or nothing matches, ( Enter the connection details myself ) when a connection has failed twice. Both are also in the overflow menu. The reply text for these is handled by the assistant calling `printer_manual_setup` or `printer_manual_connection`, which open OrcaSlicer's wizard and printer settings window respectively, then post a note with what came back.

## 5. Design details

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject
`<script>` right after `<head>` that (1) defines `window.wx` answering `hello` with
`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.
Used 2026-09-19 to review branch these-commits-are-probably-wrong in ~10 minutes.

**Why:** the desktop tools were locked by another session and background
`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming
activity line, compact photo chip, leave dialog, receipt strip) had no other cheap
proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.

**How to apply:** reach for this before building a full app + datadir copy when the
question is "what does the page draw for state X". Pair with [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]]
for the host side. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].
