content.text:
Reply posted in the thread on the card's dot and status text. Now your two questions.

**1. Discovering how to leave the setup flow.** Today there is exactly one always-visible exit: the small underlined "‹ Back" text link at the top left of the panel. The other exit is the `printer_setup_finish` tool, which the prompt says to call only when the person says they are done, "such as tapping Done". No Done is ever offered: the pinned after-add offer is "Connect it | Not now", and after "Not now" or a finished connection the reply just ends. In my three live runs no Done appeared. So a person who added a printer has no visible signal that they are finished, and a person who gave up has only a breadcrumb-style link to find.

What I would do, in order of value:

- **Have the model end the flow with a Done choice**, pinned in the prompt the same way the connect offer was pinned in 0a4d56a797: after "Not now", after a verified connection, and after "leave it for now". Tapping Done sends "Done", the model calls `printer_setup_finish`, the panel closes and the new card glows on Home. This is model-offered, so it stays inside the no-app-attached-chips rule, and the prompt test can count it.
- **Make the exit a real control**, one label, both states: a "Close" button (or an X) at the header's right, styled from the button recipe, in place of the breadcrumb link. Before a printer is added it means cancel; after, it means done. Same control, no state-dependent label.
- **Escape closes the panel**, which is what a keyboard user tries first. Today Escape does not even close the overflow menu.

**2. Undo or Remove on the "Printer added" receipt.** The receipt is a display-only block the conversation records on a successful add; it reaches the page as a block of kind "added" and never reaches the model. A button on it is app-attached UI, which is the thing you ruled out yesterday, and the handoff's decision 2 already says Undo becomes a reply the assistant offers. So the consistent design is: the model's after-add reply may include "Undo" in its choices, and saying "undo" or "remove it" makes the model call a new `printer_remove` tool.

What that takes:

- **A tool.** `printer_remove` in the registry (definition, handler enum, argument check), routed to the printer session like the other printer tools. Roughly the size of `printer_add`.
- **A backend method.** `IPrinterBackend::remove_printer` plus its Orca implementation calling `Printers::remove_named_printer`, which already exists and serves Home's "Remove printer…". The test fake backend needs it too.
- **Session bookkeeping.** Clear the session's printer name and the "already added" guard that refuses a second add of the same model, cancel any connection attempt for that printer, mark or drop the receipt block, and push `printers_changed` so Home updates.
- **Prompt and tests.** One rule for when to call it, an `agent_bridge_tests` case, and a prompt-test case if you want the offer measured.

Estimate: about 150 lines of C++ and TypeScript plus tests, half a day. The one edge to design deliberately: removing a printer that is the plater's selected preset, which Home's existing remove path already handles and this would reuse. If you would rather have a literal Remove button on the receipt despite the rule, it is smaller (a page action, a backend call, a note to the model), but it puts the app back in charge of a step the assistant is supposed to own.

> Make the exit a real control, one label, both states: a "Close" button (or an X) at the header's right, styled from the button recipe, in place of the breadcrumb link. Before a printer is added it means cancel; after, it means done. Same control, no state-dependent label.

Go with this approach. add a high prior item. Ideally we can also let the agent tell users about the everything is done, they can use "x" to close it. will this make the insutrcitons too long and confusing?

A dot in a list or card row is asked to do one of four jobs, and a good one does exactly one of them.

1. Presence or availability. The Slack, Teams and Discord dot: green means "here", grey means "away or offline", with the colour as the whole message and the word available on hover or to a screen reader. It works because every row has one, the scale is two or three values, and the meaning is stable across the app. This is the job a printer card wants: connected or not.

2. Unread or attention. The red badge dot on a tab, a mail thread, an app icon. It means "something changed here since you looked" and it disappears once you look. It never encodes a state, only novelty.

3. Activity. A pulsing or filled dot beside "Printing…", "Recording", "Live". It says a process is running now, and it is usually paired with the word or a progress bar, because the dot alone cannot say which process.

4. Severity or health in a status column. Green, amber, red beside a service name in a dashboard. This one is a three-value scale where the colours carry an order (fine, degraded, down), so it needs the same three colours everywhere and an explanation somewhere.

The rules that apply across all four: the dot is redundant with a word or a tooltip, never the only carrier (colour-blind users and screen readers); each colour means one thing app-wide; the absence of a dot must also mean something, or every row gets one; and a dot that is always the same colour is decoration and should go.

How ours measures against that. It attempts job 3 (green while printing), but the printing card already has "Printing · 43% · 2h left" and a progress bar, so the dot adds nothing there. It does not do job 1: idle-connected, unreachable and never-connected all share the same grey, which is the one distinction a person scanning the printer column wants. It is aria-hidden with no label, so it fails the redundancy rule. And since every card has one and most are grey, it reads as decoration.

So none of the four purposes is well served today. The fix is to give it job 1 and only that: green for connected (fresh data in the last 30 s), the warning colour for a printer that was verified before and is unreachable now, no dot for a printer with nothing to report (never connected, or a Wi-Fi host whose reachability the app does not track between sends), a visually hidden label with the same word the card already shows, and let "Printing" be carried by the status line and the bar, as it is now.

The status line has the same problem as the dot in a different form: it is several unrelated sentences sharing one slot. What the card can say today, from OrcaHomeBackend and PrinterCard.tsx:
- "Connected" / "Can't reach it" (Bambu device, fresh data or not), plus a Reconnect button for the second
- "Sends files over Wi-Fi" (a Moonraker/OctoPrint address is saved)
- nothing (never connected)
- "Printing · 43% · 2h left" with a progress bar, printing cards only
- "0.4 mm nozzle", printing cards only; an idle card never shows its nozzle
- the spool swatches and material label, printing cards only

So an idle Creality K1 shows one line about Wi-Fi and nothing about the nozzle, while the same printer mid-print shows four things. The line is written per situation rather than per slot.

What I would do: one grammar, every card, two lines at most.

Line 1, always present: the printer's facts, the things the person set up and would check before slicing. "0.4 mm nozzle · PLA (black)" when a spool is recorded, "0.4 mm nozzle" otherwise. Same on idle and printing cards. This is the line the printer setup conversation writes to, so it is also the receipt of what the chat did.

Line 2, only when there is a connection to report, state word first, then one fact:
- "Connected" for a Bambu device with fresh data
- "Can't reach it · last seen 2 h ago" for one verified before and silent now, with Reconnect (last message time is on MachineObject, so the age is available)
- "Sends files to 192.168.1.42" for a Moonraker/OctoPrint host, the address rather than "over Wi-Fi", because the address is what a person checks when a send fails and it is what they typed in the chat
- nothing for a printer never connected. No claim is the honest state, and it keeps the column quiet
- "Printing · 43% · 2 h left" replaces line 2 while a job runs, with the bar under it; the dot, if it stays, agrees with this line and never says more than it

Three rules behind that: the state word comes first so the column scans; each slot means one thing on every card so nothing has to be read twice; and the card never claims a connection it has not verified, which is finding 04 and is already fixed for hosts by c922876c66 (address saved only when the test passes). The one thing to add on the backend is the "last seen" age; everything else is a rearrangement of text the card already receives.

content.text:
The wireframe is implementable for Bambu printers today with mostly existing data, and only partly for Moonraker/OctoPrint printers, where Orca has no live status at all. Row by row, what the code can supply:

| Row | Bambu LAN or cloud | Moonraker / OctoPrint | Never connected |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Printing · 43%" + dot | Yes. Percent and time left come from the device's push data; "connected" means data in the last 30 s. | No. Orca never polls a print host; sends are fire-and-forget, so there is no job state to show. | No |
| Connection | Yes, reliably. Freshness from the device, and "LAN" or "Cloud" from the device's connection type. | Only "address saved and the test passed" (since c922876c66). No live reachability. Best honest line: "Sends files to 192.168.1.42". | Nothing |
| Model · nozzle | Yes. Model from the preset's `printer_model`, vendor stripped via the catalog; nozzle from the preset, or the device's own reading when connected, which already wins in the Home backend. | Yes, from the preset. | Yes, from the preset. |
| Loaded filament + swatches | Yes while connected: AMS trays give material and colour, and the external spool too if the person set it on the printer screen. Up to 4 per AMS unit. | Only what the person told the chat. Klipper has no filament colour; Spoolman is not integrated. | Only what the person told the chat. |
| Launch monitor | Yes, when connected. Opens Orca's device tab. | No monitor exists. A cheap substitute is an "Open printer page" link to the saved address, which is Mainsail or Fluidd for most Klipper printers. | No |

Three things to know before building it:

- **Home does not read the AMS today.** The printer setup conversation reads trays through `PrinterDiscovery`, which is fork code, but the Home card reads only the spool store, meaning spools the person declared in chat. So a connected X1C with four AMS colours shows nothing on its card unless someone typed them. Making Home use the same discovery path for a connected Bambu printer is a reuse, not new work, and the in-process fake Bambu printer can feed test colours through its control file.
- **The "PLA" label is currently a project fact, not a printer fact.** The card's material label comes from the project's active filament preset, shown only on the selected printer. The wireframe's "Loaded PLA" should come from the tray or spool record instead, or it will say PLA for a printer with PETG in it.
- **Live status for host printers is the one genuinely new capability.** It needs a poll of the Moonraker or OctoPrint API on a timer, new network code with its own failure modes. The Moonraker simulator on the other branch could test it, but I would not fold it into this card change. Show the saved address and leave liveness to a later step.

Reliability caveats for the Bambu column: data stops within 30 s of the printer going quiet or the app switching away from a Bambu preset, cloud printers need the Bambu login, and LAN printers need the access code, so "Can't reach it" will be a common state and the card must handle it as gracefully as "Connected".

Effort: the snapshot struct already carries state, progress, connection text, nozzle and spools. The change is adding a connection kind, a model name and the address to it, routing a connected Bambu printer's trays through discovery, and laying the card out as rows in the page. A day, with the fake printer covering the Bambu states in the harness.

Two more checks to make the answer precise: how Orca picks the Moonraker agent, and whether the fork's connect flow ever binds a Moonraker printer to it.

One more check: an older note of mine says the Moonraker agent's status stream is compiled out with #if 0 on this branch. Verifying that against the current file.

Short answer: yes for both APIs, but Orca only half-implements it, and this fork's connect flow doesn't use even that half. The quoted sentence is true of the PrintHost send path and of this fork's Home card today, but false as a statement about what Moonraker/OctoPrint allow.

What the two APIs offer

Moonraker exposes job state directly: GET /printer/objects/query?print_stats&virtual_sdcard returns print_stats.state (standby/printing/paused/complete/error), filename, durations, and virtual_sdcard.progress. It also has a WebSocket at /websocket with printer.objects.subscribe, which pushes notify_status_update on every change, so no polling is needed.
OctoPrint exposes the same through REST: GET /api/job (state, file, progress completion, printTime, printTimeLeft) and GET /api/printer (temps and state flags), both behind the API key. No push channel in the core API; a client polls.
What Orca implements in this tree

The PrintHost classes (Moonraker.cpp, OctoPrint.cpp) implement only test and upload. That is the path this fork's connect_host uses, and it really is fire-and-forget. OctoPrint.cpp only ever calls api/version; there is no api/job or api/printer anywhere in src/slic3r.
Separately, upstream added a MoonrakerPrinterAgent (src/slic3r/Utils/MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp), registered in NetworkAgentFactory alongside the Qidi, Snapmaker and Creality agents that subclass it. It has the full status machinery: query_printer_status over HTTP, a WebSocket thread that subscribes to print_stats, virtual_sdcard, heaters and fans, and map_moonraker_state into the same MachineObject state the Bambu cards use. So the code to show Idle/Printing/Offline for a Klipper printer exists.
But it is compiled out. MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp:2084-2099 wraps the initial status query and start_status_stream in #if 0 with the comment "disable websocket for now, as we don't use MonitorPanel for Moonraker printers yet". Only the connect handshake (/server/info) runs. There is no OctoPrint printer agent at all.
How that reaches the fork's Home card

GUI_App::switch_printer_agent picks the Moonraker agent only when the preset's printer_agent field says so. Vendor profiles set it for Qidi, Creality K2/SPARKX, Snapmaker U1 and OpenEYE; a generic Klipper preset, and anything this fork's connect_host sets up, has it empty and gets the plain Orca agent. connect_host writes print_host/host_type and never binds a device_id, so describe_device never runs for these printers and the card can only say "Sends files over Wi-Fi".

What it would take to show job status for Moonraker

Per my note from the jusprin-newui-fakeprinter branch, this was already done once there: flip the #if 0 to #if 1, set printer_agent=moonraker on the preset, and let the Home backend report state for a host printer whose device id matches. Screenshots there showed Idle, Printing and Offline against the Python fake. Two gotchas from that work: the agent honours enable_ssl_for_mqtt (default true) and dials https:// unless it is off, and a preset with an unparsable version is silently skipped. That branch was never merged into jusprin-newui; the #if 0 is still there.

For OctoPrint there is no agent, so it would be new code: a polling agent against /api/job and /api/printer, or accept that OctoPrint printers stay send-only.
You're right, and I should have checked the agent code rather than only the print-host send path. Verifying the claims in that side chat against this branch before I correct my assessment.

content.text:
Confirmed on this branch: the Moonraker agent with status queries, a WebSocket subscription to print stats, and the state mapping all exist in src/slic3r/Utils/MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp, and the status stream is switched off by an `#if 0` at line 2085 with the comment "disable websocket for now". OctoPrint has only the send-and-test adapter, no agent. My "No" for that row was wrong as a statement about the APIs and about the code that already exists. Corrected assessment:

**Job status for Moonraker printers: yes, with a small amount of work, none of it new protocol code.** What it takes on this branch:

- **Flip the `#if 0`** so the agent queries status and subscribes over the WebSocket. That is one edit in an upstream-owned file, so it needs the fork-stewardship justification, but it is a switch upstream left in place for exactly this purpose, and if upstream flips it themselves a rebase drops our line harmlessly.
- **Make the fork's connect path select the agent.** Orca picks the Moonraker agent only when the preset's `printer_agent` field says so, which only OpenEYE's vendor profile sets. The fork's connect writes the host address and type but never sets that field and never binds a device id, so the Home backend's device description never runs for these printers. Setting `printer_agent` to moonraker on the named printer's preset when the test passes, and binding a device id, is fork code in NamedPrinters and OrcaPrinterBackend.
- **Let the Home backend read it.** Once bound, the same code that reports idle, printing and offline for a Bambu device works, because the agent maps Moonraker states into the same MachineObject fields. The `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` branch did exactly this once against the Python Moonraker simulator, with screenshots of all three states, and was never merged. Two traps recorded from that work: the agent dials https unless `enable_ssl_for_mqtt` is off, and a preset with an unparsable version is silently skipped.

**Filament for Moonraker printers stays as I said:** Klipper reports no colour or material, so the swatches come only from what the person tells the chat unless Spoolman integration is added later.

**OctoPrint: still no job status without new code.** The API offers it, a polled job endpoint and a printer endpoint behind the API key, but nothing in Orca reads them. That would be a new polling agent, or OctoPrint printers stay send-only with the address shown.

**Effort, revised:** the card layout change stays about a day. Moonraker status on top of it is about the same again, mostly wiring and the simulator run, plus the one-line upstream flip and a note for the rebase log. I would keep the two as separate commits so the card change does not wait on the agent work.

it's ok. if for scenarios where there are no filament colors, can we can just show a downgraded version?

Yes. The row should degrade in three steps, and the rule for each step is "show what is known, never a placeholder":

- **Material and colour known** (a connected Bambu printer's AMS trays, or spools the person described with a colour): "Loaded  PLA ■ ■ ■ ■", as in the wireframe. With more than one material, the swatches carry the colours and the text names the materials: "PLA, PETG".
- **Material known, no colour** (a Klipper printer whose owner said "I loaded black PETG" without a colour the app could parse, or any spool recorded without one): the same row with the material names as text and no swatches: "Loaded  PETG". No grey placeholder square, because a grey square reads as a grey filament.
- **Nothing known:** drop the row. A card should not say "Loaded  —" or "unknown"; an absent row is the honest state and keeps the column quiet. The Model row is always present, so every card keeps at least one fact line and the rows that do appear stay in the same order, so cards still align when scanned.

Two small code consequences. The page's spool record carries only a colour today, so the wire type needs the material name added for the text form, a few lines in the snapshot and the protocol. And the spool store already allows a spool without a colour, so the text-only case exists as data now; the fake Bambu printer's control file also accepts spools without a colour, so the harness can show all three steps without hardware.

Doable, yes, and it is a small change: every state you named maps onto a boolean the Home backend already computes. Good enough, yes, with one gap to close and one known quirk to accept.

Where it maps today (OrcaHomeBackend.cpp):

Card says	Bambu (line 118)	Moonraker/OctoPrint (lines 222–227)
Online	has_recent_printer_data true (data in the last 30 s)	never
Offline	verified before (jusprin_verified_connections flag) and no recent data; keeps the Reconnect button	never
Connected	never	print_host non-empty on the preset
Not connected	no verified flag, no data	print_host empty

So it is a wording swap at those two places plus the Reconnect gating, which stays as is. No tests assert the current strings, so nothing else breaks. The vocabulary is also honest about confidence: Online/Offline is live evidence, Connected is "set up and verified once", and the shared "Not connected" means the same thing on both kinds. If the Moonraker agent's status stream is ever switched on, host printers simply move to the Online/Offline column without renaming anything.

The gap: "Connected" for a host is only true if the address was tested. The chat path guarantees that since c922876c66 (saved only on a passed test), but Orca's own printer settings dialog, reachable from the card menu and the overflow menu, saves print_host without any test. A printer configured there would read "Connected" on the strength of a typed address. Fix: gate on a verified flag for hosts too, the same jusprin_verified_connections mechanism keyed by printer name or address, set only by connect_host on pass. A few lines, and it makes the two columns symmetric: both "Connected" and "Online" require a successful contact at some point.

The quirk to accept: "Offline" for a Bambu printer means "no data in 30 s", which also happens when the app is on a different printer's preset (the agent switches away) or the person is signed out of Bambu cloud. Your standing note treats that window as normal, and it is, but "Offline" is a stronger word than "Can't reach it" for a printer that is fine. Two options: keep "Offline" and let Reconnect explain itself, or use "Offline" only when this printer's preset is the selected one and "Not connected" otherwise. # Handoff: redesign the Home printer card

Written 2026-09-24 against `jusprin-newui` at f8b2edb302. Working document: do not commit it, and do not hide it in `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Kenneth tracks unfinished work through untracked files in `git status`.

Background and the decisions below come from finding 04 of the printer setup walkthrough (https://claude.ai/artifact/Li2MEdX8tMXWqv3Hrfpepb) and the comment threads and side chats on it, 2026-09-24. Read that finding first; this file is the implementation view.

## 1. What this is about

JusPrin's Home screen lists the person's printers as cards in a column on the right (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx`, fed by `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`). Today a card's text is written per situation ("Connected", "Can't reach it", "Sends files over Wi-Fi", nothing), the dot is grey for every state except printing, an idle card never shows its nozzle, filament swatches come only from what the person told the setup chat, and a Moonraker or OctoPrint printer gets no monitor button although Orca has a Device tab for it.

The job: make every card the same shape, with every line resting on something the app has verified, and make Moonraker/OctoPrint printers first-class on it. Kenneth's wireframe:

```
[printer glyph] Bambu Lab X1C                    ● Printing · 43%
Connection      Connected · LAN
Model           X1 Carbon · 0.4 mm
Loaded          PLA  [■][■][■][■]
[ Launch monitor ↗ ]
```

## 2. Decisions already made (do not reopen)

1. **Connection vocabulary.** Bambu printers: `Online`, `Offline`, `Not connected`. Moonraker/OctoPrint printers: `Connected · <address>`, `Not connected`. The words `Can't reach it` and `Sends files over Wi-Fi` go away.
2. **Two gaps accepted.** A host printer set up through Orca's own printer-settings dialog reads `Connected` on a typed, untested address. A healthy Bambu printer reads `Offline` during the 30-second freshness window after the app switches to another preset or the person signs out of Bambu cloud. Do not add rules to paper over either.
3. **The dot means connection, nothing else.** Green for `Online` and `Connected`, the warning token for `Offline`, no dot for `Not connected`. Printing is carried by the header's job text and the progress bar, not by a dot colour.
4. **Rows degrade by omission.** A row with nothing verified to say is left out. No "unknown", no dash, no grey placeholder swatch.
5. **One action label per printer kind, not per state.** `Launch monitor` on Bambu cards, `Open printer page` on Moonraker/OctoPrint cards.
6. **Not in this change:** live job status for Moonraker printers (see section 8), any OctoPrint status agent, Spoolman, and the Bambu-side cleanup after a failed connect attempt (device stays linked and selected; separate work).

## 3. Where things are today

| File | What it does now |
|---|---|
| `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` `describe_device` (line ~99) | For a Bambu `MachineObject`: state idle/printing/offline from `machine_is_printing` and `PrinterSetup::has_recent_printer_data`; `status_text` "Printing · 43% · 2h left" and `progress_percent`; `connection_text` "Connected" / "Can't reach it" / empty using `has_verified_printer_connection`; `connection_action` "reconnect"; `nozzle_text` from the extruder system; `can_launch_monitor = connected`. |
| `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` named-printer loop (lines ~213–245) | For each `Printers::NamedPrinter`: `connection_text` "Can't reach it" if verified before, overwritten by "Sends files over Wi-Fi" when the preset's `print_host` is non-empty; `nozzle_text` from `named.nozzle`; `describe_device` when a device is bound; spools from `SpoolStore::spools_for(name)` (colour only); `material_label` from the project's current filament preset when the printer is selected. |
| `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` `launch_monitor` (line ~320) | Resolves a device id and calls `MainFrame::jump_to_monitor(device_id)`. Bambu only; a named printer without a device id returns. |
| `Home/HomeSnapshot.hpp` `PrinterEntry` | id, name, kind, can_open_settings/rename/remove, state, status_text, progress_percent, connection_text, connection_action, nozzle_text, material_label, `spools` (colour only), can_launch_monitor. |
| `Home/HomeSnapshot.cpp` (lines ~60–86) | Serialises `PrinterEntry` to the page's JSON. |
| `HomeUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts` `PrinterInfo`, `SpoolInfo` | The page's types; `SpoolInfo` is `{ colour }`. |
| `HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx` | Two layouts (idle vs printing); `status-dot` class with `printing` modifier; `printer-detail` lines; `launch-monitor` button gated on `canLaunchMonitor`, `Reconnect` on `connectionAction`. |
| `HomeUI/src/styles.css` `.status-dot` (line ~208), `.printer-*` classes | All colours are tokens (`--status-success`, `--status-danger`, `--text-secondary`); `styles.test.ts` fails the build on a literal. |
| `PrinterSetup/PrinterDiscovery.hpp` `discover_printers()` | Returns `DiscoveredPrinter` (`PrinterSetupTypes.hpp`): stable_id, name, ip_address, connection ("lan"/"cloud"), connected, activity, nozzle_diameter, ams_name, `spools` (name, material, colour) read from the device's AMS trays and external spool. Used by the setup chat, not by Home. |
| `Printers/NamedPrinters.hpp` `NamedPrinter` | name, device_id, nozzle, selected. No model name; the preset's `printer_model` config value has it (e.g. "Bambu Lab X1 Carbon"). |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/MainFrame.cpp` `show_device(bool bBBLPrinter)` (line ~1374), `load_printer_url()` (line ~4235) | Upstream. For a non-Bambu preset the Device tab is a `PrinterWebView` loaded from `PrintHost::get_print_host_webui(config)` (Mainsail/Fluidd/OctoPrint page), API key passed for PrusaLink. `tpMonitor` is the tab index. |
| `Testing/FakeBambuAgent`, `Testing/README.md` | In-process fake Bambu printer; `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` drives state, progress, nozzle, offline and `spools` (subBrands, trayType, colour optional). |

Tests that pin today's strings and shapes: `tests/jusprin/test_home_snapshot.cpp` (lines ~36–40, 110–142, 199: connection_text, spools with colour only, canLaunchMonitor), `HomeUI/src/App.test.tsx` (line ~58–61 fixture; line ~314 asserts "Can't reach it").

## 4. Target card, row by row

Fixed order. Every row is optional except the header and the Model row.

**Header.** Printer glyph, name. At the right: the dot (section 2.3) and, only while printing, `Printing · 43%` (keep `· 2h left` when known). Progress bar under the header while printing.

**Connection.** Label "Connection", value per section 2.1:

| Value | Bambu device | Moonraker / OctoPrint |
|---|---|---|
| `Online · LAN` / `Online · Cloud` | `has_recent_printer_data` true; suffix from `MachineObject::connection_type()` | never (until the Moonraker agent's status stream is enabled, section 8) |
| `Offline` (+ Reconnect button) | `has_verified_printer_connection(device_id)` and no recent data | never |
| `Connected · 192.168.1.42` | never | preset `print_host` non-empty; show the address as saved (host and port, no scheme) |
| `Not connected` | neither flag | `print_host` empty |

**Model.** Label "Model", value `<model> · <nozzle> mm`. Model from the preset's `printer_model` with the vendor prefix removed (the catalog knows the vendor: `PrinterSetup::PrinterCatalog`, see `OrcaPrinterBackend::model_of`). Nozzle: the device's reported diameter when connected (as `describe_device` already prefers), else `named.nozzle`. Always present for named printers; for a bare device (no named printer) use the device's model id and nozzle.

**Loaded.** Label "Loaded". Three steps:
1. Material names as text, then one swatch per spool, when spools have colours. Source for a connected Bambu printer: `discover_printers()` spools for the matching `stable_id` (this is what the setup chat shows; Home does not read it today). Source otherwise: `SpoolStore::spools_for(name)`.
2. Material names only, no swatches, when spools exist without a colour (the store allows an empty colour; the fake's `spools` entries may omit `colour`).
3. No row when there are no spools from either source.

The `material_label` from the project's current filament preset is removed from the card: it describes the project, not the printer.

**Action.** One button, label by kind:
- Bambu card: `Launch monitor` when `can_launch_monitor` (connected). Unchanged path.
- Moonraker/OctoPrint card: `Open printer page` when `print_host` is non-empty. New path, section 5.5.
- `Reconnect` stays where it is today (Bambu `Offline`), as a secondary action.

## 5. Implementation steps

Keep each as its own commit; 5.5 and 5.6 can land later than the rest.

### 5.1 Snapshot and protocol

`PrinterEntry` gains: `connection_kind` (`"lan" | "cloud" | "host" | ""`), `model_text`, `address`; `SpoolEntry` gains `material`. `connection_text` keeps carrying the finished string the backend writes, so the page never composes copy. Serialise them in `HomeSnapshot.cpp`; extend `PrinterInfo` and `SpoolInfo` in `protocol.ts`. No protocol version bump: additive fields (see `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` on capabilities vs versions).

### 5.2 Backend wording and gating (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`)

- `describe_device`: `connection_text` becomes `Online · LAN`/`Online · Cloud`, `Offline`, or empty; `connection_kind` from `connection_type()`. Keep `connection_action = "reconnect"` for `Offline`.
- Named-printer loop: when `print_host` is non-empty, `connection_text = "Connected · " + address`, `connection_kind = "host"`, `address` set, `can_launch_monitor = true`. When nothing applies, `connection_text = "Not connected"` for both kinds (today it is empty; the decision is to show the words).
- `model_text` from the preset's `printer_model` minus vendor.
- Spools: for a named printer bound to a device that is connected, take spools from `discover_printers()` for that `stable_id`; otherwise from the store. Fill `material`. Drop `material_label`.

### 5.3 Page (`PrinterCard.tsx`, `styles.css`)

One layout for both states: header row, optional job line and bar, then a definition-list of the three rows, then the action. Dot class from `connectionText`'s first word (or better, from a `connectionState` field if you add one in 5.1: `online | offline | connected | none`); tokens `--status-success`, `--status-warning` (add the CSS variable from the token file's `warning` if Home's `tokens.ts` does not export it yet), no element for `none`. Give the dot a visually hidden label with the same word. Swatches keep `.printer-spools`; the text-only step renders the names without the swatch elements. Every new colour, radius and size comes from the token file; `styles.test.ts` enforces it.

### 5.4 Tests to update or add

- `tests/jusprin/test_home_snapshot.cpp`: new fields serialise; a spool without colour serialises with `material` and no `colour`; a host printer carries `address` and `canLaunchMonitor`.
- `tests/jusprin/test_home_host.cpp`: wording per state for a fake device (use `FakeBambuAgent`: idle, printing, offline, and `spools` with and without colour).
- `HomeUI/src/App.test.tsx` and a `PrinterCard.test.tsx`: the four connection words, the dot class per word and absent for `Not connected`, the three Loaded steps, the two action labels, the "Can't reach it" assertion at line ~314 replaced.
- `HomeUI/src/styles.test.ts` keeps passing (no literals).
- Shell harness: extend the Home checks (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`, printer rail section around lines 497–620) to read the rail after connecting the fake Bambu printer and after saving a host address through the setup chat's connect flow (the `--printer-connect-capture` mode from c013c97942 already produces a connected host printer against a loopback listener).

### 5.5 `Open printer page` for host printers

In `OrcaHomeBackend::launch_monitor`, add a branch for a named printer with no device id and a non-empty `print_host`: select that printer's preset if it is not the selected one (this changes the open project's printer; that is Orca's own Device-tab behaviour and the label sets the expectation; if the project is dirty, Orca's usual preset-switch prompt applies), then `m_frame.show_device(false)` if the web view is not built, `m_frame.load_printer_url()`, and select `MainFrame::tpMonitor`. All three are existing upstream calls; do not change `MainFrame`. Verify against a loopback HTTP server that serves a page (the harness's connect-capture listeners can serve a body), and note that a host that is off shows a blank tab: that is the accepted `Connected` vs `Online` gap made visible.

### 5.6 Fixture for screenshots

For page-only review, the fake-host page fixture recipe (memory note "fake-host-page-fixture") renders `resources/jusprin/home/index.html` under a scripted `window.wx`; the walkthrough's `home-host.js` in the session scratchpad shows the state shape. Under Playwright it can save PNGs.

## 6. Verification before calling it done

1. `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target jusprin_web` after every page edit, or the app serves a stale bundle.
2. `jusprin_tests` (home snapshot and host), `shell_integration_harness` default mode, HomeUI Vitest, all green.
3. Live: shell harness with the fake Bambu printer in idle, printing, offline, and with/without spool colours; one Moonraker host connected through the setup chat against a loopback listener; screenshots of each card state in light and dark (`--dark-ui`).
4. `git status` shows only intended files; this handoff stays untracked.

## 7. Risks

- **Preset switch on `Open printer page`.** Changing the selected printer from Home can mark the project dirty or trigger Orca's preset-switch dialog. Test with a dirty project open.
- **`discover_printers()` cost.** It walks the device list; Home rebuilds its snapshot on every device event. Measure before calling it per card; cache per snapshot build if needed.
- **30-second window.** `Offline` will appear on healthy printers briefly; accepted, but the harness check must wait past the window (memory note "printer-setup-connect-means-verify-and-save").
- **Token coverage.** `--status-warning` may not exist as a CSS variable in Home yet; adding it goes through `tokens.ts` and the token file, never as a literal.

## 8. Follow-on, not in scope: live status for Moonraker printers

Orca ships `src/slic3r/Utils/MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp` with `query_printer_status`, a WebSocket subscription to `print_stats`/`virtual_sdcard`, and `map_moonraker_state` into the same `MachineObject` fields the Bambu cards use. The status stream is compiled out at line ~2085 (`#if 0`, "disable websocket for now"). Orca selects that agent only when the preset's `printer_agent` field says `moonraker` (only OpenEYE's vendor profile sets it), and the fork's `connect_host` sets neither that field nor a device id. Enabling it means: flip the `#if 0` (an upstream-file edit; justify per `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`), set `printer_agent` on the named printer's preset when the test passes, bind a device id, and let `describe_device` run. The `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` branch did this once against the Python Moonraker simulator; two traps recorded there: the agent dials `https://` unless `enable_ssl_for_mqtt` is off, and a preset with an unparsable version is silently skipped. OctoPrint has no agent at all. With it enabled, host cards move to `Online`/`Offline` with no wording change.

result.output:
Replace saved spools with a filament chip built on Orca's own slots

The header chip remembered a "spool" per printer -- a filament preset, a
colour and a name -- and seeded one from the open project whenever a
printer with none was selected. Home then showed that seed as "Loaded" on
printers nobody had described, and the setup chat stored the model's
material word where a preset name belonged. The spool concept is gone
(turn 23 of the Prepare wireframes): the chip and its menu now read and
write only what OrcaSlicer already keeps.

- Chip: printer nickname and nozzle (each size when they differ), then
  one dot per project slot -- faded when the current plate does not print
  with it, unused slots folded into "+n" past eight, dots shrunk when more
  than eight are in use -- and the filament's short name when the used
  slots share one, otherwise a count. The rules live in FilamentChipModel,
  which jusprin_tests covers without wx.
- Filament menu: a colour row (the slot's colour, Orca's saved colours,
  "+" for the system picker), the installed filaments that fit in
  brand-then-name order, Other filament... (Orca's own filament page),
  Filament settings... and Add a slot. It stays open, so a filament and a
  colour change in one visit. With several slots a slot list opens first.
  "Use what's loaded on the printer..." leads only when the printer
  reports trays, greyed with the reason while it is offline, and runs
  Orca's own sync unchanged.
- A filament change follows Orca's colour rule (a preset with a default
  colour brings it; otherwise the slot keeps its colour), through one
  per-slot SetupCommands path the Agent's filament change now shares.
- One grey thread line per menu visit that changed a filament, led by the
  colour it landed on; notes gain an optional swatch for that. A
  colour-only visit adds no line.
- Home's Loaded row shows only trays a connected printer reports.
  printer_change saves the nozzle only, and the setup chat is told what is
  loaded only from the printer itself.
- A nozzle change on the project's printer runs the compatibility pass
  Orca's printer switch runs, so a process or filament made for the old
  nozzle is replaced. That is a real change to the project, and the
  harness now expects the project to be modified exactly when something
  was replaced (it was the opposite rule from 7f66e75b07).

The fake Bambu printer can now send a tray's filament id, as hardware
does: Orca's sync skips a tray without one, so without it the sync could
not be exercised.

Verified on Windows: jusprin_tests 52 cases, agent_bridge_tests 258,
jusprin_fake_bambu_tests 10, AgentUI 204 and HomeUI 61 Vitest tests. Shell
harness: --printer-setup 166 checks and --home-live 70 checks pass (the
tray row opens Orca's sync with the sidebar hidden, and the two fake trays
land in the project's slots); the default run passes 433 of 434, the
exception being print_opens_cancellable_native_preflight, which fails the
same way on this machine without these changes.

No OrcaSlicer-owned file is touched.

input.text:
Half right, and "longer term" was the wrong label. The tools exist and the mechanism is all there; what they cannot do today is reach a printer preset. Checked in the code:

- Scope. settings_search is titled "Search process settings" and requires an active FFF process preset. The adapter reads and writes presets->prints (the process preset). Nothing reads the printer preset's settings.
- Target. The optional target argument accepts only {objectId}, for printing one object differently. There is no way to say "the printer preset" or to name a printer.
- What may be written. SettingsSupport.hpp has an allowlist of about forty keys, all process keys (layers, walls, infill, supports, brim, seam, ten speeds). No retraction, no machine limits, no bed size, no start G-code. Each key on that list was traced through Orca's normaliser and handlers first, which the tool guide requires.
- Who can call them. They are exposed to the project conversation and to MCP. The printer conversation has its own list of eight printer_* tools and does not get them.

So extending them is reuse, not new design. What it takes:
1. A scope argument (process | printer) on the four settings tools. The guide already planned "scope and target as optional fields".
2. The adapter reading and writing a printer preset by name. The printer conversation is about a named printer that may not be the selected preset, and the tools act on whatever is selected today.
3. An allowlist of printer keys, each traced the same way. This is the real work: some printer settings rewrite others or raise Orca dialogs (nozzle changes run the compatibility pass, for one). Start with the handful people ask for.
4. The tools added to the printer session's list, with the approval card the panel already draws for printer_connect's kind of call.

Size: the plumbing in 1, 2 and 4 is about a day. Item 3 scales with the number of keys, roughly an hour or two per key for tracing and a test. A first cut with retraction length, z-hop, and the machine speed and acceleration limits is a two to three day job.

Finding 07 now says "Next: extend the settings tools that already exist" with this list (report version 14).

input.text:
Sorry, that reply used my own shorthand. Here it is in plain words.

OrcaSlicer keeps three kinds of saved settings:
- printer settings (bed size, retraction, speed limits, start G-code)
- filament settings (temperatures, flow)
- process settings (layer height, walls, infill, supports, print speeds)

The assistant already has tools to search settings, read them, and change them with a preview and an approval card. But those tools only ever look at the third kind, process settings. They cannot see or change printer settings at all. That is the whole gap.

"Scope" was my word for "which of the three kinds of settings the assistant is asking about". Today there is no choice, it is always process settings. The change is to let the assistant say "printer settings" when it calls the same tools.

"Target" is an option those tools already have. It means "apply this change to this one object only, not the whole print", for example printing one part with more infill than the others. It only accepts an object. I brought it up because it cannot be used to point at a printer, so a separate way to name the printer is needed: the printer conversation can be about a printer that is not the one selected in the open project.

So, to let people change printer settings by talking, four things are needed:
1. Let the assistant ask for printer settings instead of process settings.
2. Let it say which printer, by name.
3. Decide which printer settings it may change, and check each one for side effects in OrcaSlicer first. The assistant may change about forty process settings today, and each of those was checked this way. This is most of the work.
4. Give the printer conversation's assistant access to these tools. Today only the project conversation's assistant has them.

I rewrote that paragraph in finding 07 the same way (report version 15).
